coding.note: CodeGen is a released model family. Claims consolidate repeated abstract/introduction statements; no new architecture or training-method contribution is claimed there, so C2 is NA throughout. Sampling temperatures, generated samples, and standard errors over problems do not establish independent training seeds. Comparator evaluation is mixed: MTPB comparators were evaluated by the authors, while starred HumanEval and MBPP comparator results were copied. Third-party is coded NO because no independent evaluation of CodeGen itself is reported; copied comparator evaluations are recorded separately. Data disclosure is PARTIAL: sources, language-level sizes, and preprocessing are given, but the exact GitHub selection/mixture is not reconstructible. Corpus token counts and training batch sizes/steps are disclosed; hardware is described without duration or total compute. Prior techniques retain their existing names, so no clear renames are coded.

scores_copied.quote: Results for the model marked with ∗ are from Chen et al. (2022).

claims.quote:
To democratize this, we train and release a family of large
  language models up to 16.1B parameters, called C ODE G EN, on natural language
  and programming language data
claims.claim: Train and openly release the CodeGen family, up to 16.1B parameters, for program synthesis.

claims.quote: We study multi-turn program synthesis emerging in autoregressive models under scaling laws.
claims.claim: Study the emergence of multi-turn program synthesis as model and data scale.

claims.quote: We leverage this capacity to introduce a multi-turn program synthesis paradigm.
claims.claim: Introduce multi-turn program synthesis by progressively specifying subproblems in natural language; demonstrate improved synthesis over single-turn specifications.

claims.quote: We investigate its properties quantitatively with a novel multi-turn programming benchmark.1
claims.claim: Introduce MTPB, a novel benchmark of 115 problems for quantitative multi-turn program synthesis evaluation.

claims.quote:
For scaling the training, a custom library JAX FORMER for TPU-v4 hardware was developed
and will be released as open-source, including the trained model weights.
claims.claim: Develop and open-source the custom JAXFORMER training library for scaling models on TPU-v4.

claims.quote:
We show the utility of the trained model by demonstrating that it is competitive with
  the previous state-of-the-art on zero-shot Python code generation on HumanEval.
claims.claim: Demonstrate competitive zero-shot Python code generation against the previous state of the art on HumanEval.

data_disclosure.quote:
The multi-lingual dataset B IG Q UERY is a subset of Google’s publicly available BigQuery dataset,
which consists of code (under open-source license) in multiple programming languages.

In the MTPB, each problem has 5 test cases and we sample 40 samples
for each test case with each model, based on which the pass rate is computed for each problem.
